newsitem.title: USA: Philips - Lucent venture a good fit.
newsitem.headline: Philips - Lucent venture a good fit.

text.p: The $2.5 billion consumer products joint venture planned by Philips Electronics NV and Lucent Technologies Inc is a perfect geographic fit between the two companies.

Philips is the leading maker of corded and cordless phones in Europe and has a growing presence in Asia. Lucent is the top supplier of corded and cordless phones and answering machines in the United States.
"The only overlap is upside," said Michael McTighe, managing director of Philips's consumer electronics arm and the chief executive of the new venture.
As an example of the venture's expected synergies, McTighe said Lucent's line-up of phone products primarily sold in the United States could be targeted at selected overseas markets.

"There are many markets in Latin America and Asia where we can offer those products in a short period of time," he said. The products meet U.S. Federal Communications Commission requirements, which would smooth their entry into new markets, he said.
At the same time, executives stressed that the venture will continue to execute existing strategies in the two companies' respective product and geographic markets.
McTighe said the only major country where neither company has significant operations is Japan, but the new venture has its eye on that country in the coming year.
"Probably the only country we won't see anything in this year is Japan," he said. "Next year we will attack there."
Both the existing Philips consumer unit and the new venture are known as Philips Consumer Communications.
The venture will initially be based in Parsippany, N.J., near Lucent's Basking Ridge, N.J., headquarters, while a search for a permanent base takes place, officials said.
The executives said the new venture took shape quickly after talks began two to three months ago. The lack of overlap in the companies' operations proved to be a catalyst, they said.
The venture brings together the $1.4 billion consumer products business of Philips and the $1.1 billion Lucent consumer product business.
Ownership of the venture -- 60 percent by Philips and 40 percent by Lucent -- represents the approximate revenue contribution of the two companies, a Lucent spokeswoman said.
Carly Fiorina, a respected Lucent executive who recently took the helm of the company's consumer products business as president, will serve on the board of the new venture.
She said Lucent's U.S. market share was double that of any rival in corded and cordless phones and answering machines.
Reuters interviewed McTighe and Fiorina by telephone today.
